reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 0, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the November 2025 date chart. What day of the week is November 4?
Look at the January 2025 date chart. What day of the week is January 10?
Look at the July 2025 date chart. What day of the week is July 17?
Look at the May 2025 date chart. What day of the week is May 14?
Look at the February 2025 date chart. What day of the week is February 13?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample requires reading a specific calendar chart to determine a day of the week for a stated date, e.g. seed 43's 'Look at the January 2025 date chart. What day of the week is January 10?', directly matching 'determine the day...of the year using a calendar'.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names determining both 'day and month' using a calendar, but all five samples only ask 'what day of the week is [date]'; none asks the student to determine or state a month from the chart, so only half the named pairing is exercised.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The recurring stem 'Look at the [Month] [Year] date chart. What day of the week is [Month] [Day]?' stays under 15 words in every sample, e.g. seed 46's 13-word version, and is a single calendar-lookup step appropriate for Grade 1 Quarter 4.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All five samples share the identical sentence template and differ only in the substituted month/day/year values; no alternate framing, such as asking what date falls on a given weekday, appears across the sample set.

competency_alignment.rationale: Variation is confined to different months, November, January, July, May, February, and target dates, directly building calendar-lookup skill without drifting into date arithmetic.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Real calendar dates spanning five different months of 2025, days 4 through 17, are concrete, grade-appropriate real-world values for a Grade 1 calendar-reading competency.
